title: A GLD premium at the New York close is a metal purchase in London tomorrow: the authorised participant has already locked its spread and must settle in physical, price-insensitively, into the LBMA auction

scout.mechanism: SPDR Gold Shares creates and redeems in baskets of physical gold, not cash. When GLD's market price closes above its indicative value, an authorised participant sells GLD short against the premium and commits to deliver metal into the trust; the arbitrage profit is locked at that moment, and what remains is an OBLIGATION to source bullion in London within the settlement cycle. From that instant the AP is a price-insensitive buyer: it has already been paid, so it is optimising for certainty of settlement rather than for price, and it sources at the benchmark because the trust itself values at the LBMA auction price. Redemptions run the same machinery in reverse. The forcing event is therefore observable BEFORE the metal is bought, and it is published: the SPDR archive carries, per day since 2004-11-18, the closing price, the indicative value and the mid-market quote at 16:15 New York, the resulting premium/discount, and the total ounces held by the trust. The premium is the trigger; the change in ounces is the completed flow, reported that evening. The claim is that the day-t premium (and its sign and size) predicts gold's return in the LONDON hours of day t+1, when the AP must actually buy. This is a mechanism and not a signal because the trader whose behaviour is being predicted has no discretion: the basket is already committed and the metal has to exist in a vault.
scout.why_unarbitraged: The published tonnage is universally quoted, but as SENTIMENT — 'ETF holdings rose, investors are buying gold' — on a weekly or monthly chart. The tradable content here is the settlement plumbing, not the sentiment: a premium at 16:15 New York is a claim on metal at a London auction the next day, and the only participants who see that obligation in real time are the APs themselves, who are already trading it and whose activity is the reason the effect should be small rather than absent. Everyone else sees the number after the US close. Why the residual survives being known: (1) it is a one-day hold worth single-digit basis points, and at institutional size in London gold the market impact of trading it exceeds the effect — it is genuinely too small for anyone with real capital, which is the brief's own example of a valid answer; (2) the AP's obligation is contractual and cannot be withdrawn if it becomes crowded, so unlike an information edge it cannot be traded away by the forcer changing behaviour; (3) assembling it is annoying — the archive is an XLSX behind an API endpoint whose plain-CSV URL currently serves a PDF, and it must be joined to a London-clocked intraday gold series across sixteen years of DST, which is exactly awkward-rather-than-secret. Honest weakness, stated here rather than left for the adversary: the AP may source from an existing vault position or an EFP rather than in the auction, and to the extent it does, the flow never touches the window being measured. That is the most likely way this dies.
data_needed: SPDR GLD historical archive — VERIFIED REACHABLE TODAY, one download: https://api.spdrgoldshares.com/api/v1/historical-archive?product=gld&exchange=NYSE&lang=en returns an XLSX whose 'US GLD Historical Archive' sheet has 5,692 daily rows, first row 18-Nov-2004 (8.09 tonnes) and running to the present, with columns Date, Closing Price, Ounces of Gold per Share, NAV/Share at 10:30am NYT, Indicative Price per Share at 4:15pm NYT, Mid point of bid/ask spread at 4:15pm NYT, Premium/Discount at 4:15pm NYT, Daily Share Volume, Total Ounces of Gold in the Trust, Tonnes of Gold. The plain-CSV URL that search engines return (assets/dynamic/GLD/GLD_US_archive_EN.csv) serves a 120-page PDF and must not be used. Needs an ingest script and a pinned local copy under data/etf/ with the fetch date in its header, to this repository's usual provenance standard.

data/bars/XAUDUKA-1m.parquet — ON DISK: 5,635,777 gold minutes, 2010-06-01 to 2026-05-31, flat bars already dropped. Overlaps the archive on roughly 4,000 trading days, which is fifteen to twenty times the sample of any news-conditioned record in this repository.

data/bars/XAUUSD-1m.parquet — ON DISK: the broker's own minutes, 2026-06-02 to 2026-09-11, for a recent-year confirmation read under the owner's 2026-09-13 criterion (docs/decisions/2026-09-13-recent-year-screen.md).

Vantage costs, already measured and already in config: spread 0.28 on XAUUSD.sc, and the account is swap-free (config/default.toml records 340 closed positions, 87 held overnight, swap 0.00). A one-day hold therefore costs 0.28 on a ~4,300 price, about 0.65 bp round trip — the cost the effect has to clear, and it is unusually low for an overnight claim.

A London clock. The LBMA gold auctions are 10:30 and 15:00 London; the existing docs/decisions/2026-09-13-london-fix.md study already built the 09:30-10:00 New York window for the afternoon auction and its drift null, so the window, the control and the receipt format are reusable and only the conditioning variable is new.
scout.falsifier_sketch: Declare before the run: the conditioning variable is day-t Premium/Discount at 16:15 New York (a published number, known before any London hour of day t+1 opens); the statistic is the MEDIAN day t+1 return over the afternoon-auction window, taken separately in the top and bottom quintiles of the premium; the declared direction is that a top-quintile premium precedes a HIGHER return than a bottom-quintile premium, with no mirror available. It dies if the difference in medians is <= 0; if it is positive but fails the 95th percentile of a null that permutes the premium across days within the same calendar month (so the gold trend cannot supply it — the standing objection from 2026-09-15-venue-residual, where a book 73% long in a year gold rose 37% earned +0.587 bp of bull market); or if the day-block bootstrap interval declared alongside the percentile straddles zero. Three further pre-declared conditions, each of which closes it on its own. (1) Placebo window: the same test on the 10:30-11:00 New York hour, which contains no auction, must NOT produce the same effect. (2) Placebo lag: day t's premium must not predict day t-1's window; if it does, the premium is a proxy for the recent trend and this is momentum. (3) The completed-flow arm: the change in Total Ounces reported for day t must predict day t+1 in the same direction and with the same sign as the premium arm, since the two are the trigger and the completion of one obligation; if the tonnage arm is flat while the premium arm works, the mechanism named here is not what produced the number. Draws at 100,000, per the standing precision rule in BACKLOG.md, and the guards from config/default.toml applied to the trade list, since a measurement whose sign flips under this project's own limits is not a candidate for anything.
scout.closest_known: docs/decisions/2026-09-13-london-fix.md — the UNCONDITIONAL hold into and out of the LBMA afternoon auction, which closed at the 84th and 74th percentile of the drift null with PF 0.961 and 0.904 on 578 holds. That record is the closest relative and it is also the argument for this one: it tested whether the auction window drifts at all and found it does not, which is what you would expect of a window whose flow is two-sided on an average day. It never asked whether the SIGN of that window is knowable in advance from a published measure of who is obliged to buy there. The distinction is exactly the distinction the loop drew on 2026-09-14 between a calendar and a release: a window is not a mechanism, an obligation is. Second closest: docs/decisions/2026-09-14-pre-nfp-drift.md and 2026-09-15-nfp-cross-asset.md, the only other records that condition an intraday gold window on an external published quantity. Those condition on a scheduled release, where the information arrives DURING the window; this conditions on an obligation created the previous evening, where the information is fully public and only the execution is still to come — which is why it does not collide with the news blackout that forbade trading the pre-NFP hour.

verdicts.note: No decision record covers ETF creation/redemption, authorised-participant settlement, fund flows, or any gold window conditioned on a published premium; across all 38 records, the backlog and both syntheses the only hit for GLD/ETF/creation/redemption is a reopening clause, not a closure. The scout names 2026-09-13-london-fix.md correctly and the naming holds: that record asked whether the LBMA afternoon window drifts UNCONDITIONALLY (PF 0.961 / 0.904 on 578 holds, 84th and 74th of the drift null; 0.935 / 0.932 on 1,401 holds in the addendum) and never asked whether the window's sign is knowable in advance. A shared window is not a shared mechanism, which is exactly the distinction this gate is for. One citation the scout missed and should carry: 2026-09-13-btc-us-hours.md's “what would reopen this” names “a different window with a reason (e.g. the ETF creation/redemption window)” — the desk nominated this family once, on a different asset, and never tested it, so this is the first asking, not the second. Two warnings from the file. First, london-fix's own reopening clause reads “tick data around 10:00 New York with the actual auction timestamps, on a cost below $0.10. Not more days of five-minute bars”; this proposal is not that, it is a different question inside the same window, and the registration must say so in one sentence, because a conditional cut inside a window already measured flat is one selection step away from a re-run of the parent. Second, see my note on 2026-09-15-monthend-hedge-rebalance: that proposal and this one are one mechanism on two benchmarks, they share this same closest relative, and they must be accounted for as one degree of freedom rather than two independent tests.

The conditioning variable is not on this disk. There is no data/etf/ directory and nothing under data/ holds a GLD series; this session has no web access, so the 5,692-row XLSX is an assertion in the proposal rather than a file anyone here has opened - and the proposal itself records that the URL search engines return serves a 120-page PDF instead of the CSV it advertises, which is exactly the kind of claim that has to be verified by download before anything is built on it. The work to lift this is bounded and worth naming: somebody with a browser fetches the archive once; it is pinned under data/etf/ with the endpoint and the fetch date in a header, to the standard docs/news/README.md sets; an ingest script parses the 'US GLD Historical Archive' sheet (openpyxl 3.1.5 is installed, xlrd is not, so it must be .xlsx), validates the Premium/Discount column's units by recomputing it from closing price and indicative price, and joins the daily rows to a London/New York clock across sixteen years of DST. Four to six hours after the file arrives; unbounded until it does. The expensive half is on the disk and I measured it: data/bars/XAUDUKA-1m.parquet is 5,635,777 minutes, 2010-06-01 -> 2026-05-31, 4,972 sessions of at least 200 bars, of which 4,110 carry at least 25 of the 30 minutes of the 09:30-10:00 New York window that docs/decisions/2026-09-13-london-fix.md already built for the afternoon auction. Quintiles of roughly 820 days each - the largest sample of the four proposals by an order of magnitude, and the reason this is the fetch worth doing. Cost is also the friendliest of the four: the live probe in data/spreads/XAUUSD_sc.csv (998 samples, 02:01-07:32 UTC on 2026-09-15) reads a p50 spread of 0.21 dollars, 0.49 bp, against a claimed single-digit-bp effect, so for once the claim is not smaller than its own round trip. One caveat the registration must state rather than discover: the recent-year read cannot use data/bars/XAUUSD-1m.parquet, which is capped at 100,000 bars and covers only 2026-06-02 -> 2026-09-11; a daily-frequency recent-year confirmation has to come off XAUUSD-15m (2022-06-16 -> 2026-09-11), which gives about 250 days, quintiles of 50, and will not resolve a single-digit-bp effect on its own.
